cycles.summary: Finalized an unplanned-but-approved skill authored by a previous worker. The SKILL.md, references (cancellation-decision-guide, complaint-template) and the offline cancellation-fee.py script already existed; this cycle added the Hebrew-facing SKILL_HE.md, metadata.json, evidence.json, and this optimization log to match the standard Lawcal legal-tech skill package. Ran the calculator smoke tests (fee cap, defective=0, refund deadline). No claims were fabricated; fee caps and exclusion lists that change are flagged verify-current in the body.

changes.detail: Added SKILL_HE.md: Hebrew RTL mirror of the English instructions, examples, gotchas, reference links and troubleshooting.
Added metadata.json (author, version 1.0.0, category, bilingual tags + display name/description, supported agents).

Added evidence.json documenting 10 claims sourced to the Consumer Protection Law 5741-1981, the 2010 cancellation regulations, the Consumer Protection Authority pages, Kol Zchut, and the local calculator check.
Verified scripts/cancellation-fee.py: price 3000 -> fee 100 (5%=150 capped); price 1000 -> fee 50; --defective -> fee 0; refund deadline = notice + 14 days. stdlib only.

deferrals.reason: The bitul-iska exclusion list and the NIS 100 fee cap are amended periodically. Per anti-fabrication, the skill presents the current list and cap with an explicit verify-current instruction rather than asserting them as permanently fixed.
